correctness.rationale: Let t be the number of distinct syntactic subformulas in a BALFI nonvalid formula. The Boolean algebra generated by those values and top is finite; greedily choose ≤t atoms distinguishing all |S|≤t+1 relevant elements. Coordinate projection is a Boolean homomorphism injective on S. Thus prescribed N and C outputs at occurring whole argument vectors remain functional; when missing N defaults to complement, and missing C defaults to bottom, which preserve x∨N(x)=top and x∧N(x)∧C(x)=bottom jointly even if one entry was previously prescribed. Structural induction preserves falsification. Guess t vectors of length m≤t and check binary functions, whole-vector unary collisions and all mixed N/C constraints in polynomial time; established coNP-hardness gives coNP-completeness. Explicit 2-coordinate BALFI with N=(3,3,1,0), C=(0,0,0,3), p=1,q=3 refutes (p↔q)→(Np↔Nq), though all 1-atom BALFIs validate it. Independently checked truth table and constraints. No claim that t is an optimal lower bound.
